ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Jean-Jacques Rousseau Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for beliefs of being plotted against, poor sleep, and difficulty passing urine. Concerns: Cannot pass urine freely: a thin stream, straining, burning, and the feeling of never emptying; fears the passage will one day close completely; dilates himself with urethral sounds every few days; Sleeps four hours a night and lies awake going over what his former friends are doing to his name; Wants to be believed and not called mad, to read his own records, and to decide for himself; has little trust in doctors. [S]

Two tablets up to every 8 hours as needed
Aripiprazole 5 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth each morning
Ibuprofen 400 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth three times a day with food for up to seven days
One tablet three times a day with food

tr.td: Kidney, ureter, and bladder ultrasound: normal kidneys without hydronephrosis; bladder wall thickened to 6 mm with trabeculation; post-void residual 190 mL; prostate 24 mL
Retrograde urethrogram: a 1.5 cm ring-like narrowing of the proximal bulbar urethra with a lumen of about 8 French; penile urethra normal; no false passage or diverticulum
Voiding cystourethrogram: the bladder neck opens normally; the posterior urethra is dilated above the bulbar narrowing; no reflux; bladder trabeculation

Flexible cystourethroscopy: meatus normal in position and size (no hypospadias); a pale, dense ring of scar in the proximal bulbar urethra that the 16 French scope could not pass; no tumor or stone seen below it

Bulbar urethroplasty by excision and primary anastomosis, his informed choice: 1.5 cm of dense spongiofibrosis excised and the ends joined; 16 French urethral catheter left in place. Pathology: dense fibrosis of the corpus spongiosum without inflammation or malignancy
Pericatheter retrograde urethrogram three weeks after urethroplasty: no leak at the anastomosis; catheter removed and he voided well

Delusional disorder, persecutory type (DSM-5-TR), of about nine years' duration, with non-bizarre beliefs of a coordinated campaign against him; no hallucinations, disorganization, or mood episode; normal cognition; insomnia secondary to preoccupation; synthetic modern counterpart of his documented persecutory beliefs: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Primary care visit for beliefs of being plotted against, poor sleep, and difficulty passing urine
Psychiatry consultation and review of the urethral imaging and cystoscopy
Seven-week review of psychotherapy and safety, and preparation for urethroplasty
Review four weeks after urethroplasty; start of aripiprazole
Same-day sick visit for low back pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Engagement without confrontation: listen to his account in full, acknowledge his distress and the real conflicts in his life, neither argue with nor agree with the beliefs, and agree shared goals that matter to him (sleep, less distress, freedom to write, and his bladder); give him copies of his results and notes

Look for medical, substance, and neurocognitive causes: neurological examination, MoCA, blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, TSH, and vitamin B12; review of medicines and alcohol; brain imaging only if the course or examination is atypical

Psychiatry consultation to confirm the diagnosis and the differential, assess the risk of harm to himself and others, advise on an antipsychotic and on cognitive behavioral therapy for psychosis, and assess his capacity to consent to urethral surgery

Structured suicide and violence risk assessment with a written safety plan and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; no firearms in the home; risk reviewed at every visit; signs for urgent care written down with him

Urology assessment: IPSS, uroflowmetry, bladder scan for post-void residual, urinalysis, and creatinine now, and kidney and bladder ultrasound this week; retrograde urethrogram, voiding cystourethrogram, and flexible cystoscopy by the urology team next week; stop self-dilation with urethral sounds (urethral rest) and come in the same day if he cannot pass urine
Right inguinal hernia: watchful waiting while it is minimally symptomatic, with the warning signs of incarceration explained; reassess once the straining has been relieved
Sleep: fixed rising time, daylight walks, no writing about his enemies after 8 pm, and no sedating antihistamines or anticholinergic sleep aids, which can worsen urinary retention

Cognitive behavioral therapy for psychosis with the clinic psychologist, about 16 weekly to fortnightly sessions, aimed at distress, worry, sleep, and checking and safety behaviors rather than at disproving the beliefs

Antipsychotic offered by shared decision-making: aripiprazole 5 mg daily recommended, for its low anticholinergic, sedative, and metabolic effects; he declined it at the consultation and the offer stays open; no compulsory treatment while he remains safe

Bulbar urethroplasty by excision and primary anastomosis, his choice after dilation, internal urethrotomy, and self-catheterization had been explained; urethral rest until surgery; capacity to consent confirmed; catheter for three weeks with a pericatheter urethrogram before removal; acetaminophen rather than opioids afterwards

Aripiprazole 5 mg each morning, started at his request; weight at 4, 8, and 12 weeks then quarterly; blood pressure, fasting glucose or hemoglobin A1c, and lipids at baseline and 12 weeks then yearly; waist at baseline and yearly; akathisia check at each visit; AIMS at baseline and every 6 months
Surveillance after urethroplasty: symptoms and IPSS, uroflowmetry, and post-void residual at about 3, 6, and 12 months; urethroscopy or a urethrogram only if symptoms return or the flow falls
Sleep at least six hours most nights
About six and a half hours most nights by twelve weeks on aripiprazole
Less distress and preoccupation from the beliefs, so that he can write each morning and walk without fear
Preoccupation down from most of the day to under an hour; writing most mornings; the beliefs persist with less conviction
Stay in care: keep visits and psychotherapy sessions, with no sudden break in treatment
Kept every visit and fourteen of sixteen CBT sessions
Pass urine with a free stream without self-dilation: maximum flow above 15 mL/s and post-void residual below 100 mL within three months of surgery
Maximum flow 20.8 mL/s and residual 30 mL four months after urethroplasty; no sounds used since January
No harm to himself or anyone else; safety plan kept current
No suicidal or violent thoughts at any visit; safety plan reviewed at each visit

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; writing daily; has stopped seeing most acquaintances and opens no letters from people he suspects [S]
Alert and oriented; neatly but plainly dressed; courteous, watchful, and guarded at first, warmer once he felt heard; speech fluent, faster and louder on the subject of his enemies [S]

Mood "hunted and tired"; affect anxious and at times tearful; thought process logical, detailed and circumstantial on the theme of the plot; fixed, non-bizarre beliefs that former friends, publishers, and the people around him are coordinating a campaign to defame him and are opening his mail and messages, held with full conviction; no hallucinations; no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone; insight into the beliefs absent, insight into his urinary illness good; MoCA 28; Insomnia Severity Index 18 (moderate) [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1767-01-20: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with a two-week follow-up. He has persecutory beliefs but no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone, no plan to confront or act against the people he fears, no command hallucinations, and no access to firearms, so he does not need hospital care. Risk factors reviewed: a persecutory delusion, insomnia, social isolation, chronic pain on passing urine, male sex, and a past thought of suicide after a painful accident many years ago. Signs for urgent care were written down with him (thoughts of harming himself or anyone else, planning to confront someone, not sleeping at all for two nights, or a sudden urge to leave his home). A written safety plan was made with him, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
